picks.producer: Union of Winemaking Cooperatives of Samos
picks.why: The growers' co-operative union founded in 1934, the appellation's only producer until 2016 by Wines of Greece, with wineries at Malagari and Karlovasi; Samos Vin Doux, small grained White Muscat fortified with grape spirit, is the bottle any server meets.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS; the region record's producers line names the house, a lead and no proof. Confirmed in the thin run: 1934 on the co-operative's own history page (samoswine.gr, read through search) and at Wines of Greece, which adds that it began with twenty six local co-operatives and that it was the only producer of the appellation until 2016, private wineries working beside it since; the island's wine routes guide names its two wineries, at Malagari by the town of Samos and at Karlovasi. Samos Vin Doux is listed under that name by a British magazine and a Canadian critic. The house's name differs by source: Union of Vinicultural Cooperatives of Samos (EOSS) at Wines of Greece, United Winemaking Agricultural Cooperative of Samos or UWC Samos in the wine routes guide and on the listings; the pick keeps the name the region record uses: give the name the label prints, and say when the union took its later form only if two sources date it. Wines of Greece gives the appellation three types: vin naturellement doux from sun dried grapes, vin doux naturel, fortified, with Grand Cru for fruit grown above 400 metres, and vin doux; that the Vin Doux is a vin de liqueur, fortified at or near the start of fermentation, rests on the region record and one taster's note: confirm it on the appellation's specification. Grand Cru, Nectar, of sun dried grapes, and Anthemis, aged in oak, go in others. Shares, volumes and exports stay out.

picks.why: Family winery at Karlovasi, opened in 2013 by the island's wine routes guide and a merchant's account, of a family that came from Malta in the nineteenth century and traded the island's Muscat; Nopera Vintage is its sweet Samos of sun dried Muscat.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not in the region record's producers line. Confirmed in the thin run: the island's wine routes guide (samoswineroutes.gr, read through search) places the winery at Karlovasi, dates its opening to 2013 and tells of a family that left Malta in the middle of the nineteenth century, made wine of White Muscat on Samos and later traded it abroad; a merchant's page also gives 2013, as the year the house became the first modern private winery. No page of the house's own was reached: hedge the family's story as the house's account, and leave founded empty unless 2013 stands on the house's own page. That it was the first private winery of Samos since 1934 is the guide's and that merchant's line, and Vakakis is dated 2011: hedge it or leave it out. Nopera Vintage is sold under that name by a Greek merchant (the 2013) and by a British importer of Greek wine (the 2017: ripe Muscat dried in the sun, then fermented slowly), and listings place it under PDO Samos; a Greek Master of Wine's site lists it as Nopera with the year alone and gives the 2014 about two years in French oak, and a British magazine lists it as Nopera, Samos: give the label in full for the year taught and confirm the appellation on it. Epitome, the house's other sweet wine, and Roya, its dry Muscat, which the lane held to be a wine of geographical indication outside the sweet appellation, go in others; confirm what Epitome is, since one listing runs it together with the Vintage of 2013, and confirm Roya's category. The guide's three vineyards and their size stay out. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Private winery near Karlovasi that began in 2011, while the law of 1934 still bound the island's growers to the co-operatives; Epogdoon, its Samos of partly sun dried White Muscat, is named for the interval of nine to eight in the Pythagorean theory of music.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not in the region record's producers line. Confirmed in the thin run: two accounts, a Greek merchant's and a tour guide's, date the house to 2011, when the law of 1934 still obliged the island's growers to deliver their grapes to the co-operatives, and say its founder fought that rule in the Greek and the European courts: tell the lawsuit only with a source that names the case, and say what the house bottled before 2016, which no search showed. The village differs by source: the island's wine routes guide places the winery at M. Lakka, on the road from Karlovasi to Konteika, and a travel guide files it under Vathy: follow the wine routes guide. Epogdoon is listed as PDO by a British merchant (the 2016, Muscat Blanc alone) and under Samos on a British critic's site (the 2017, there called Pythagorean Epogdoon Barrel): a barrel aged bottling stands beside the plain one, so say which is taught and give the label in full. The name, by the Greek merchant quoting the house: the epogdoon is the interval of nine to eight on which the Pythagorean theory of music rests, chosen for a partly sun dried wine of White Muscat; the same page says about eight kilos of fruit give one litre: confirm both on the house's own page. The lane's line that the house is known for reviving Black Muscat was not tested: say it only with two sources. Filion, listed under Samos on the same critic's site, and Kalypso go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Small family winery at Marathokampos, at work since 2016 among the terraces of the family's estate; its Samos, sold under the appellation's name alone, is a naturally sweet wine of sun dried White Muscat aged at least three years in barrel, by the house's account.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not in the region record's producers line. Added in the thin run as the fourth pick. Confirmed on the house's own pages (coutsodontiswinery.gr, read through search): small lots made since 2016 on a family estate at Marathokampos among traditional terraces; the wine is headed Samos Naturally Sweet Wine in English and Samos, oinos fysikos glykys, in Greek, the 2017 of Muscat Blanc from small terraces at 100 to 300 metres, the grapes laid in the sun before pressing, fermented in stainless steel and aged at least three years in barrels. The island's wine routes guide also dates the family winery to 2016 and places it at Marathokampos. No merchant, critic or competition listing of the wine was found, so the record would rest on the house's pages alone: hedge every figure as the house's account. The letters PDO were not seen: the page gives the appellation's name and the legal words for its sun dried type, which Wines of Greece lists under PDO Samos, so confirm the appellation on the label before the record says it. The pick holds Samos alone because the wine has no other name: give the label in full. Its dry White Muscat, its aged dry White Muscat, its orange wine and its pétillant naturel go in others: confirm each one's category, since none can be the sweet appellation's wine. The house writes Coutsodontis; a Greek news guide writes Koutsodontis. No listing off the island was found: the record says plainly that this is a small young house, little seen abroad on what was read. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Young family estate at Mytilinii in the centre of the island, founded in 2019, farming organically and making only White Muscat, dry and naturally sweet; Anavasis is the wine it bottles as Samos, young and from a wild ferment by a merchant's listing.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not in the region record's producers line. Added in the thin run as the fifth pick, and the one in doubt. Confirmed: the island's wine routes guide (samoswineroutes.gr, read through search) dates the winery to 2019 at Rizovrachos, Mytilinii, in central Samos, a father and his two sons working organic vineyards and making only dry and naturally sweet wines of White Muscat in numbered bottles; the estate's own page (hatziioannouestate.gr, read through search) calls it a family house given wholly to organic wines. Anavasis: the results of the Concours Mondial de Bruxelles list Hatziioannou, Samos, Anavasis 2021 as a still wine of Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains, appellation Samos, organic and not oaked; a wine app names it Samos with the wine's name in Greek; a delicatessen that sells the island's wines online lists Anabasis in a half litre bottle as an organic Samos, young and fermented by native yeasts alone. No page read says PDO or sweet of this wine outright: the case rests on the name Samos on the label, which only the appellation's wine may carry, on the competition's appellation field, on the half litre bottle and on the estate's naturally sweet wines. Confirm on the estate's own page or the label that Anavasis is PDO Samos and which of the appellation's types it is; if it is not, the pick falls. Antamoma, also written Rendezvous, its dry White Muscat, goes in others. The spelling is Anavasis at the competition and Anabasis at the delicatessen; the house is Hatziioannou on its own pages and Hatzigiannou in a Greek news guide, and a retailer's dry Muscat of Chatziioannou Domaine may be the same estate or another house: keep them apart until shown. The medal stays out. Name no living member of the family. Should the pick fall, no sixth house of the appellation was found: of the seven the wine routes guide lists, Kostaki, whose first vintage was 2023, makes dry and sparkling Muscat by a Greek merchant and a British magazine, and nothing was found on the wines of Eleftheriou at Stavrinides; the Samos bottled by the mainland houses Kourtaki and Cavino, seen in Canadian listings, was not tested and is a label from off the island.
